terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. run.js starts the cupboard server, runs your functions against it and prints every request and answer.

tasks.title: Read a value from the question mark part
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/search.js`, make `queryValue(address, name)` give back the value called `name` in the question mark part of `address`, decoded the way the server reads it: `'Mabli & the Moths'`, not `'Mabli+%26+the+Moths'`. When there is no value with that name, it gives back `null`.

Check calls `queryValue` with an address of its own whose values have encoded characters in them, and with a name that is not there.
nextSteps: Make a `URL` from the address and print its `searchParams`.
Ask `searchParams` for the value by its name.
Try a name that is not in the address and look at what comes back.
Run `node run.js` and compare the two Task 1 lines with the address they read.
hints: Cutting the text at `?`, `&` and `=` yourself leaves the codes like `%26` and `+` in the values. `URL` decodes them for you.
A `URL` has a `searchParams` property that holds the names and values of the question mark part, already decoded. Its `get` method gives back `null` for a name that is not there.

tasks.title: Build a search address
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `searchAddress(base, artist, title)` give back, as text, the address of `/songs/search` on the server at `base`, with `artist` and `title` in the question mark part. Both must reach the server exactly as they were typed, with any `&`, `#`, `+`, `%` or space in them. When `title` is not given, the address has no `title` at all.

Check calls `searchAddress` with artists and titles of its own, reads the address back the way a server does, and compares each value with what was typed.
nextSteps: Make a `URL` for the search page from `base`, as in the last issue.
Put the artist into its `searchParams` and print the address.
Put the title in only when it was given.
Run `node run.js` and read how `&` and `+` look in the address.
hints: Building the question mark part with a template literal puts an `&` or a `#` from a value straight into the address, where it means something else.
`searchParams` has a `set` method that adds a name and value and encodes the value for you. A parameter that was not given is `undefined`.
Make `const url = new URL('/songs/search', base)`, call `url.searchParams.set('artist', artist)`, do the same for title inside `if (title !== undefined)`, and return `url.href`.

tasks.title: Search the cupboard server
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `searchSongs(base, artist, title)` send a request for that search to the server at `base`, wait for the answer, and give back the text of its body. `title` may be left out here too, and then the request has no title.

Check starts a server of its own, calls `searchSongs`, and looks at both sides: the artist and title its server read from the request, and the text `searchSongs` gave back.
nextSteps: Get the address of the search from the function you wrote in Task 2.
Send a request there with `fetch` and wait for the answer.
Read the body as text, wait for it, and give it back.
Run `node run.js` and read the first line of each answer: it says what the server looked for.
hints: This is Task 2 and the last task of the previous issue put together.
A function can call another function of the same file. Hand `searchAddress` the three values `searchSongs` was given, even when the title is `undefined`.
`const response = await fetch(searchAddress(base, artist, title))`, then give back the body text, waited for with `await`.

tasks.title: Ask for the next page
tasks.description:
The server shows two songs at a time. Under `// Task 4`, make `nextPage(address)` give back, as text, the same address with `page` one higher. An address with no `page` is on page 1, so its next page is 2. Every other value stays as it was, and `page` appears only once.

Check calls `nextPage` with addresses of its own, with and without a page, and reads every value of the address it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the page out of the address and print what kind of value it is.
Decide what the page is when the address has none.
Work out the next page as a number, and put it back in place of the old one.
Run `node run.js`: the server should answer with the next two songs.
hints: Every value in the question mark part is text, even when it looks like a number, and `'9' + 1` is `'91'`.
`Number()` turns text into a number. `get` gives `null` for a name that is not there, and `set` replaces a value that is already there instead of adding a second one.
Read it with `Number(url.searchParams.get('page') ?? '1')`, then `url.searchParams.set('page', String(page + 1))` and return `url.href`.
